questions.q: Why should each project get its own virtual environment?
options: Python refuses to run without one
Different projects need different package versions, and a private environment keeps an upgrade in one from breaking another
It makes Python code execute faster
It is required before you can import the standard library
questions.explain: An environment holds a private copy of the interpreter and its own installed packages, so projects do not interfere with each other's versions.

questions.q: Which command creates a virtual environment in a folder named .venv?
options: pip install .venv
python --version .venv
python -m venv .venv
pip freeze > .venv
questions.explain: python -m venv .venv runs the venv module and creates the environment folder. You then activate it.

questions.q: What does pip freeze > requirements.txt do?
options: Locks the environment so no more packages can be installed
Deletes unused packages
Uninstalls every package in the environment
Writes every installed package and its exact version to a file so the environment can be rebuilt
questions.explain: pip freeze lists installed packages with pinned versions; redirecting it to requirements.txt records them, and pip install -r requirements.txt rebuilds the same set.

questions.q: You activated an environment. How can you tell from the terminal?
options: The prompt shows the environment name, such as (.venv), in front
The terminal window closes and reopens
Python prints a confirmation banner every time you type a command
Nothing changes; there is no visible sign
questions.explain: Activating an environment prefixes the prompt with its name. Type deactivate to leave it.

questions.q: What should you commit to version control for a project's Python setup?
options: The entire .venv folder
Only the requirements.txt file, not the .venv folder
The Python installer
Nothing; environments cannot be shared
questions.explain: The environment folder is large and machine-specific. requirements.txt is a small recipe anyone can use to rebuild it.
